claims.text: Pew 2023 (24 countries; fieldwork 20 Feb-22 May 2023, US 20-26 Mar): medians calling each system good: representative democracy 77%, direct democracy 70%, rule by experts 58%, strong leader 'without interference from parliament or the courts' 26%, military rule 15%; majorities reject strong-leader rule in all but five countries; strong-leader support up in 8 of 22 since 2017, down in Hungary, Israel, Italy and Sweden

Pew 2023 topline Q42c, very or somewhat good for a strong leader: US 26, Canada 19, UK 31, France 12, Germany 16, Italy 20, Spain 17, Netherlands 12, Sweden 5, Greece 13, Poland 25, Hungary 15, Israel 19, Australia 20, Japan 33, South Korea 35, India 67, Indonesia 51, Kenya 52, Nigeria 43, South Africa 47, Argentina 27, Brazil 36, Mexico 50

Pew short read: support for strong-leader or military rule (either) median 31% across 24 nations, India 85% highest, Sweden 8% lowest; higher on the right in most of 18 countries (South Korea right 49%, centre 36%, left 28%); UK below-median income 47% vs 27%; US under-30s 38%, 50-64 29%, 65+ 26%

Afrobarometer (18 Jul 2024; 39 countries; 53,444 interviews): 66% prefer democracy; 80% reject one-man rule, 78% one-party rule, 66% military rule; 53% would accept a military takeover if elected leaders abuse power; opposition to military rule down 11 points over a decade in 30 countries
Latinobarómetro 2026 (presented 2 Oct 2026; 18 countries): support for democracy 52%; authoritarian government preferable 17% (16% in 2024); highest Argentina 73%, lowest Guatemala 35%, Brazil 41%

de36_china.topic: China's social credit system: what it is and what it is not

claims.text: Daum (2018): 'there is no score' in the holistic sense; PBOC credit reporting gives a data sheet; system = financial credit, industry-specific regulatory blacklists, moral education; joint punishment through inter-agency MOUs; the 2014-2020 Planning Outline is a planning document, not a law; a few local pilots score people with mild consequences; Shanghai app voluntary; enforcement mainly targets companies and reaches 'the actual controller, even primary shareholders'
Judgment-defaulter list: coercive, 'you can get off of that by paying'; bans on flights and the best trains; criticised because 'it treats all court judgments as equal' (Daum)

National Public Credit Information Center 2018 report (AP via CBC): flight purchases blocked 17.5 million times and train 5.5 million times in 2018; 128 people barred from leaving the country over unpaid taxes; 290,000 instances blocking senior management or legal-representative roles

NDRC (SCMP 2019): 20.47 million plane and 5.71 million high-speed rail tickets blocked; 13.49 million individuals on the court list at end of March 2019; also barred from financial markets, premium insurance, wealth products, property; some localities exposed personal information
SPC (China Daily 28 Jan 2026): number on the defaulter list declined in 2025 after a first drop in 2024; courts held 4,461 people criminally accountable in 2025 for refusing to comply with rulings

HRW (12 Dec 2017): journalist Liu Hu lost a 2015 defamation suit, paid the court-ordered apology, later found he could not buy plane tickets; court said payment not received; still blacklisted; HRW: courts 'failed to notify them, leaving them no chance to contest'; 'there is nothing wrong about authorities enforcing legitimate court orders'; punishments imposed 'more than seven million times' by 2017

Freedom House CMB 133 (Feb 2019): in Rongcheng a petitioner was docked 950 points after sending more than 1,000 online appeal letters; a community penalised 'illegally spreading religion'; Weibo 'Sunshine Credit' lets users report 'untrue information'

31 March 2025: CPC Central Committee and State Council General Offices issued 23 measures to improve the social credit system with 'unified rules and regulations', citing inconsistent frameworks and weak sharing, and calling for protection of information security and individual rights

EU AI Act prohibited practices, including a ban on using AI to score individuals on social, personal or professional behaviour where it leads to unfair or disproportionate treatment (Art. 5(1)(c)), applied from 2 Feb 2025, penalties from 2 Aug 2025; Commission guidelines 4 Feb 2025
